Location: Riverside Community Library, 42 Oak Street, Springfield

Why Join Page Turner?

Thoughtful Discussions

Engage in meaningful conversations about books you love with readers who share your passion for storytelling and exploring new perspectives.

Diverse Selections

From literary fiction to mystery and memoir, we choose a variety of genres each year. Members vote on upcoming selections to ensure everyone has a voice.

Community Connection

Meet like-minded book enthusiasts in your neighborhood. Our club welcomes readers of all levels and backgrounds who love to read.

Monthly Gatherings

Join us once a month to discuss the book, share snacks, and enjoy the company of fellow readers in a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere.

Ready to Turn the Page?

No pressure, no fees—just book lovers gathering to celebrate the stories that move us. Whether you've already finished this month's pick or you're just curious, we'd love to see you at our next meeting.

What We're Reading

Our current selection and upcoming discussion

The Midnight Library

by Matt Haig

Published: 2020
Pages: 304
Genre: Contemporary Fantasy, Philosophy

Synopsis

Nora Seed finds herself in a library that exists between life and death, between the person she is and the person she might have been. With the help of a librarian, she explores parallel lives and alternate choices, discovering what truly matters and what makes a life worth living.

A magical and moving story about second chances, regret, and the infinite potential within us all.

Discussion Themes

Choices and Regret

How does Nora's journey through parallel lives change her perspective on the choices she's made? Are there moments in the book that made you reconsider your own life decisions?

The Meaning of a Good Life

What does the Midnight Library suggest about what makes a life meaningful? Does success or happiness look different to each of the book's versions of Nora?

Connection and Relationships

How do Nora's relationships with others evolve throughout the story? Which character had the most impact on her journey, and why?

Regret and Acceptance

By the end of the book, how has Nora's relationship with her own life changed? What does she learn about acceptance and moving forward?

Our Next Meeting

Saturday, January 18th, 2025

Time: 2:00 PM – 4:00 PM

Location: Riverside Community Library, 42 Oak Street, Springfield

Room: Community Room B (ground floor)

Join us for lively discussion, refreshments, and good company. Whether you've finished the book or just started, all perspectives are welcome!

Join or RSVP

How We Choose

Our current book was selected by club members through a democratic voting process. We choose a diverse mix of genres and styles throughout the year—from literary fiction to science fiction, mysteries to memoirs—ensuring every reader finds something to love.

Interested in suggesting a book for our next selection? Members can nominate titles for the next voting round. Join us to have your voice heard!

Meeting location: Riverside Community Library, 42 Oak Street, Springfield

Home Current Book Past Meetings Join Us

Past Meetings

Explore the books we've loved, the discussions we've shared, and the stories our members have told.

Our Reading Journey

The Midnight Library

November 2024

by Matt Haig

A woman on the brink of giving up gets a chance to explore parallel versions of her life, discovering hope and possibility in unexpected places.

Members present: 12

Discussion highlight:

"Nora's journey reminded us that regret doesn't have to define us—every choice matters, but so does the chance to try again." — Sarah M.

Remarkably Bright

October 2024

by Katherine Allsopp

A coming-of-age story about a brilliant teenage girl navigating school, friendship, and finding her voice in a world that often silences young women.

Members present: 14

Discussion highlight:

"We all saw ourselves in Maya's struggle to be heard. This book sparked the best conversation about belonging we've had all year." — James T.

The House in the Cerulean Sea

September 2024

by TJ Klune

A caseworker for magical creatures visits an orphanage on a remote island and discovers that acceptance and love are the most powerful magic of all.

Members present: 11

Discussion highlight:

"A feel-good masterpiece. We laughed, we teared up, and we left the meeting believing in kindness again." — Marcus L.

Lessons in Chemistry

August 2024

by Bonnie Garmus

Set in the 1960s, a female chemist fights discrimination and discovers her voice while hosting a cooking show, changing both her life and television history.

Members present: 13

Discussion highlight:

"Elizabeth's determination inspired us all. We talked about how far we've come and how far we still need to go." — Patricia K.

The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo

July 2024

by Taylor Jenkins Reid

A reclusive Hollywood icon reveals the secrets of her glamorous past to an unknown magazine reporter, uncovering love, betrayal, and fierce ambition.

Members present: 15

Discussion highlight:

"We couldn't stop talking about the twists! This book had us guessing until the very last page. Absolutely unputdownable." — Devon R.

Verity

June 2024

by Colleen Hoover

A struggling editor uncovers shocking truths while ghostwriting the memoir of a famous author, leading to a psychological thriller with an unforgettable ending.

Members present: 12

Discussion highlight:

"The unreliable narrator had us debating what was real for hours afterward. Brilliantly crafted and deeply unsettling." — Lisa W.

pages.title: Join Us – Page Turner Book Club
pages.html:
📚 Page Turner
Home Current Book Past Meetings Join Us

Join Us

We'd love to have you at our next meeting! Page Turner Book Club is open to readers of all levels and interests. Whether you're a voracious reader or just looking to explore new books, there's a place for you here.

Membership & Benefits

Free to Join

There are no membership fees. Book club is open to everyone in the community.

Monthly Discussions

Join us for thoughtful conversations about the books we read, sharing different perspectives and insights.

Book Recommendations

Discover new titles, genres, and authors recommended by fellow readers who share your passion for books.

Community Connection

Make friends with fellow book lovers and build lasting connections over our shared love of reading.

Meeting Schedule

Frequency: Second Thursday of every month

Time: 7:00 PM – 9:00 PM

Format: In-person discussions with optional virtual attendance available

Our meetings typically last about two hours and include informal refreshments. No need to rush through the book—we focus on enjoying the experience together.

Location & Directions

Riverside Community Library
42 Oak Street
Springfield

We meet in the Community Room on the second floor. There is free parking available in the library lot, and the building is accessible to all visitors.

For first-timers: ask at the front desk and they will direct you to our meeting room. Feel free to arrive a few minutes early to meet other members!

Ready to Join?

Fill out the form below and we'll send you details about our next meeting and add you to our mailing list.

We'll never share your information. By signing up, you consent to receive emails about upcoming meetings and book selections.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I have to read the entire book before coming?

Not necessarily! We encourage you to read as much as you can, but even if you just read part of the book or come with questions, you're welcome. Some members listen to audiobooks on their commute, others read a few chapters—everyone participates at their own pace.

What if I miss a meeting?

No problem! Our book selections are announced well in advance, so you can join whenever works for you. We also send monthly email reminders with book details and meeting information.

Can I bring a guest?

Absolutely! Bring a friend or family member. We love welcoming new people, and it's a great way to introduce others to our community.

Do you have a reading list for the year?

Yes! We publish our selections three months in advance so you can plan ahead. Check back on our website or ask us at the meeting and we'll send you the full year's list.

I'm nervous about speaking up in groups. Is that okay?

Listening is just as valuable as sharing! Our discussions are casual and welcoming. No one is forced to speak, and you can participate in whatever way feels comfortable. Many of our members start by listening and gradually share more as they get to know the group.

© 2024 Page Turner Book Club. All book lovers welcome.

Email: hello@pageturnerclub.local | Phone: (415) 555-1234

Meeting location: Riverside Community Library, 42 Oak Street, Springfield
